content.text:
**With `provider: "kernel"`, Kernel supplies payment credentials; the website’s existing payment processor charges the user’s card.**

For Clanker, the flow would be:

1. **User clicks “Pay ₹69” in Slack.** First time, they open Kernel’s private enrollment page and enter their card and email. Keeping that wallet enables future reuse. [Kernel wallet contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)

2. **Clanker creates a purchase-specific card item** tied to that wallet, merchant, amount and currency. Kernel obtains a network token number, expiry and one-time three-digit payment code. **Visa requires a separate passkey approval; Mastercard has no hosted purchase approval.** [Purchase contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

3. **Kernel fills those credentials into the merchant’s checkout.** Clanker then submits the website’s normal Pay button. This native flow uses browser field filling—not the blog’s browser-egress substitution mechanism. [Native card behavior](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

4. **The merchant processes the payment.** If the bank requests OTP/3DS, our private user handoff must handle that, then resume checkout.

5. **Clanker verifies the paid order and posts confirmation in Slack.** Kernel explicitly does **not** observe whether the merchant charged the card, so successful filling alone cannot mean “payment completed.” [Confirmation boundary](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

That is the published workflow. Whether our Kernel project, the user’s card and a particular merchant actually support it still needs a live test.

**Yes—the route you’re describing is how Kernel’s native card flow is intended to work: use Zepto’s “Add New Card.”**

**No special Zepto integration with Clanker or Kernel is documented.** Kernel supplies card credentials to the existing checkout, and Zepto’s own checkout submits the payment. [Kernel’s native card contract](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

For the screen you shared:

1. Clanker selects **Credit & Debit Cards → Add New Card**.
2. Kernel fills a **network-token card number, expiry and one-time three-digit code**, representing the user’s enrolled card.
3. Clanker submits payment; the user completes any required bank authentication.
4. Clanker verifies Zepto’s paid-order confirmation.

**“Kernel wallet” is our backend connection to the user’s card.** It doesn’t mean selecting PhonePe or Amazon Pay under Zepto’s “Wallets” section.

Your reasoning is right: **using existing card fields makes the checkout approach reusable across websites.** The remaining uncertainty is whether each merchant’s payment processor accepts Kernel’s generated credentials. Your screenshot proves Zepto offers card entry; it doesn’t prove that acceptance. We still need a real compatibility test before saying Zepto works.

# Native Kernel card purchases

Clanker uses `provider: kernel` wallet/card items and the merchant's existing
**Pay by card / Add New Card** checkout. AgentCard and Link are not involved.
This implementation is local; no gateway restart, real enrollment or charge has
been performed. Provider/project access, Indian issuer eligibility and Zepto
acceptance remain unverified.

1. In the requester-owned private task, inspect the card checkout and bind the
   visible item summary, INR total, HTTPS page, browser and final Pay button.
2. Deliver a private **Pay ₹X** Slack card. The authenticated review page freezes
   those facts and accepts approval plus a remember-card choice. No card fields
   are accepted by Clanker. Kernel hosts card/email enrollment and Visa approval.
3. Poll advertised eligibility and create/authorize one purchase-specific card.
   Resume through the existing durable gateway path when ready.
4. Fill through Kernel and click the bound Pay button once. Bank OTP collection
   uses a private Kernel credential form, with a separately bound verification
   page/button. Neither a fill nor a click is payment success.
5. Resolve only a visible merchant receipt with explicit paid status, matching
   amount and an order ID. Remove a temporary wallet after resolution; failed
   removal blocks reuse and is retried. Remembered wallets remain owner-bound.

The initial implementation supports INR/India and the provider's 50,000-minor-unit
limit (₹500). Hosted approval links are validated against `vault.kernel.sh`.
Uncertain mutations/submissions remain durably claimed and are not replayed.
Cancellation closes an unsubmitted purchase's browser before retiring its token;
it cannot cancel or refund a potentially charged order.

Ordinary browser tools are blocked while filled payment fields might remain,
including cross-origin frames. The payment status tool reads only restricted
page text/control metadata, never input values or screenshots. The current bank
challenge discovery and receipt selectors rely on observable page DOM; arbitrary
cross-origin bank challenges, non-English receipts and real merchant behavior
still require acceptance testing. An unsupported challenge stays unresolved.

Verification uses real local request/HTTP stores and frontend JavaScript with
synthetic provider/browser I/O; it is not evidence of a real payment:
